import pandas as pd

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
source6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/training_6.csv", index_col=0)
source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/training_7.csv", index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source6_19_0", "Source6_19_1"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 2) JOIN : [["Source6_19_2", "Source6_19_3"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
join_2_3 = pd.merge(source2, source3, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 3) JOIN : [["Source6_19_4", "Source6_19_5"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
join_4_5 = pd.merge(source4, source5, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 4) JOIN : [["Source6_19_7", "Source6_19_0"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
# Note: source0 already loaded, join with source7
join_7_0 = pd.merge(source7, source0, on="Artist", how="inner")

# 5) JOIN : [["Source6_19_6", "Source6_19_7"], ["Artist", "Artist"]]
# join source6 with source7
join_6_7 = pd.merge(source6, source7, on="Artist", how="inner")

# Now we have these intermediate joins:
# join_0_1: Artist, Score, Albums in RS500
# join_2_3: Artist, Top 100 Singles, Highest Position, Times on Cover of RS
# join_4_5: Artist, Influenced, Certified Units (Millions)
# join_7_0: Artist, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated, Score (from source0)
# join_6_7: Artist, Spotify, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated

# We need to combine all these into the final target table:
# Target Schema:
# ['Artist': string,
#  'Year Inducted': float,
#  'Years Waited': integer,
#  '# of Years Nominated': integer,
#  'Influenced': integer,
#  'Certified Units (Millions)': float,
#  'Albums in RS500': integer,
#  'Top 100 Singles': integer,
#  'Highest Position': integer,
#  'Times on Cover of RS': integer,
#  'Score': float,
#  'Spotify': integer]

# Strategy:
# - join_7_0 and join_6_7 share Artist, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated
#   We will merge join_7_0 and join_6_7 on Artist, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated
#   to get Spotify and Score (from source0) and Year Inducted etc.
# - join_0_1 has Score and Albums in RS500, but Score is also in join_7_0 and join_6_7.
#   Since join_7_0 and join_6_7 have Score and Spotify, and join_0_1 has Score and Albums in RS500,
#   we will merge join_7_0 with join_0_1 on Artist and Score to get Albums in RS500.
#   But join_7_0 already has Score from source0, so merging on Artist is enough.
#   However, join_7_0 and join_0_1 both have Score from source0, so merging on Artist is sufficient.
# - join_2_3 has Top 100 Singles, Highest Position, Times on Cover of RS
# - join_4_5 has Influenced, Certified Units (Millions)

# Step 1: Merge join_7_0 and join_6_7 on Artist, Year Inducted, Years Waited, # of Years Nominated
merged_7_0_6_7 = pd.merge(
    join_7_0,
    join_6_7[['Artist', 'Spotify']],
    on='Artist',
    how='outer',
    suffixes=('', '_y')
)

# Step 2: Merge merged_7_0_6_7 with join_0_1 on Artist to get Albums in RS500
merged_with_0_1 = pd.merge(
    merged_7_0_6_7,
    join_0_1[['Artist', 'Albums in RS500']],
    on='Artist',
    how='outer'
)

# Step 3: Merge with join_2_3 on Artist to get Top 100 Singles, Highest Position, Times on Cover of RS
merged_with_2_3 = pd.merge(
    merged_with_0_1,
    join_2_3[['Artist', 'Top 100 Singles', 'Highest Position', 'Times on Cover of RS']],
    on='Artist',
    how='outer'
)

# Step 4: Merge with join_4_5 on Artist to get Influenced, Certified Units (Millions)
final_merged = pd.merge(
    merged_with_2_3,
    join_4_5[['Artist', 'Influenced', 'Certified Units (Millions)']],
    on='Artist',
    how='outer'
)

# Now final_merged should have all columns, but some columns may have duplicates or suffixes
# Check for duplicate columns and drop if any
# There might be a 'Score_y' column from merge suffixes, drop if exists and keep 'Score'
if 'Score_y' in final_merged.columns:
    final_merged.drop(columns=['Score_y'], inplace=True)

# Reorder and cast columns to match target schema and types
# Target Schema:
# ['Artist': string,
#  'Year Inducted': float,
#  'Years Waited': integer,
#  '# of Years Nominated': integer,
#  'Influenced': integer,
#  'Certified Units (Millions)': float,
#  'Albums in RS500': integer,
#  'Top 100 Singles': integer,
#  'Highest Position': integer,
#  'Times on Cover of RS': integer,
#  'Score': float,
#  'Spotify': integer]

# Cast columns to correct types, handling missing values appropriately
def to_int_or_nan(series):
    return pd.to_numeric(series, errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

def to_float_or_nan(series):
    return pd.to_numeric(series, errors='coerce').astype(float)

final_df = pd.DataFrame()
final_df['Artist'] = final_merged['Artist'].astype(str)

final_df['Year Inducted'] = to_float_or_nan(final_merged['Year Inducted'])
final_df['Years Waited'] = to_int_or_nan(final_merged['Years Waited'])
final_df['# of Years Nominated'] = to_int_or_nan(final_merged['# of Years Nominated'])
final_df['Influenced'] = to_int_or_nan(final_merged['Influenced'])
final_df['Certified Units (Millions)'] = to_float_or_nan(final_merged['Certified Units (Millions)'])
final_df['Albums in RS500'] = to_int_or_nan(final_merged['Albums in RS500'])
final_df['Top 100 Singles'] = to_int_or_nan(final_merged['Top 100 Singles'])
final_df['Highest Position'] = to_int_or_nan(final_merged['Highest Position'])
final_df['Times on Cover of RS'] = to_int_or_nan(final_merged['Times on Cover of RS'])
final_df['Score'] = to_float_or_nan(final_merged['Score'])
final_df['Spotify'] = to_int_or_nan(final_merged['Spotify'])

# Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_19/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
